Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (T/T47/T47n1998A.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Dahui Pujue. Dahui Zonggao owns the retained deployment: takes up the hawk-shooter's arrow through the red sun's shadow in hall, asking whether before the arrow leaves the bowstring there is any news of it at the shadow's edge, and once it has left, where this news lands, for whoever knows the landing-place breaks three passes with one arrowhead and sees the road behind the arrow, and whoever does not had better hide back under the crossbow.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X72/X72n1432.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Wuming Huijing. Wuming Huijing owns the retained deployment: asks his hall what ascending the hall and entering the room amounts to, only for the old man of the west who faced the wall nine years without preaching, invites whoever has it to step out, and when the head seat stays seated and answers that a poor house shows the filial son and a state in trouble shows the loyal minister, rules the words not lacking but asks where Damo's intent lands, taking the white clouds flying sea and peak and bringing a skyful of gloom.

Linye Tongqi owns the retained deployment: on the arrival of a fellow master in days of falling snow, raises in hall that flake after flake does not fall anywhere else and asks where it lands, for to say it falls on the ground has not left ordinary feeling, and to say it does not fall on the ground leaves it nowhere to come down, and so with incense held straight they bow and ask the guest to show it.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J39/J39nB449.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Zuliangqi. Zuliang Chaoqi owns the retained deployment: in memory of his late teacher who held the mountain, built the cloister and set its rules by the true mind, himself relying on that mind to enter the teacher's hall and room, hangs that one true mind on the head of his staff for the brothers to lift their brows and see, each attesting it and being its beam and pillar, then asks where after all so many true minds land, Phoenix Mountain abrupt from past to present and the true dharma unbroken ten thousand years.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J40/J40nB494.xml). Recorded Sayings of Monk Yushan. Yushan Shangsi owns the retained deployment: asked in the evening assembly where Huangbo's staff lands, answers with the sky-leaning long sword that chills a man, and when the monk calls that the ancients' own, returns the demand, telling him to say where it lands, and when the monk answers it lands at Linji's, strikes him across the back for having forgotten himself.

Senses.Explanation: The demand masters put to a shout or a staff-blow the instant it is spent, asking where the thing came down. Dahui Zonggao takes up the hawk-shooter's arrow through the red sun's shadow and asks whether, before the arrow leaves the bowstring, there is any news of it at the shadow's edge, and once it has left, where does this news land, for whoever knows the landing-place breaks three passes with one arrowhead and sees the road behind the arrow, and whoever does not had better hide back under the crossbow, Wuming Huijing asks his hall what ascending the hall and entering the room amounts to, only for the old man of the west who faced a wall nine years without preaching, and when the head seat answers that a poor house shows the filial son and a state in trouble shows the loyal minister, rules the words not lacking but asks where Damo's intent lands, Miyun Yuanwu verses a sick monk through rounds of cold and heat that no medicine cures until the white sweat breaks and ease returns, sings it again today and shows it to the monk with the whip pulled tight, then asks where the whip-head lands, and Linye Tongqi, snow falling for days on the visit of a fellow master, sets flake after flake not falling anywhere else and asks where it lands, for to say it falls on the ground has not left common feeling and to say it does not leaves it nowhere to come down. Tian'an Sheng hears the night compared to Yangqi opening a stall and scattering pearls no account outdoes, and turns to old Pang bowing out of Yaoshan's door saying good snow, flake after flake, not falling elsewhere, and since it does not fall elsewhere, he asks where after all it lands, for whoever knows the landing can sit on Pang's tongue and whoever does not will be laughed at by Puxian riding the white tiger, Tianyin Yuanxiu, the monk shouting after the ninety days' knots, grants it a good shout and asks where it lands, the monk shaping a palm-blow and the master answering the monk still owes him a slap, Zuliang Chaoqi hangs the true mind with which his late teacher held the mountain, built the cloister and set its rules, on the head of his staff for the brothers to see, each to attest it and be its beam and pillar, and then asks where after all so many true minds land, Phoenix Mountain abrupt past to present and the true dharma continuing ten thousand years, and Yushan Shangsi, asked where Huangbo's staff lands, answers with the sky-leaning long sword that chills a man, and told that is the ancients' own, returns the demand, you say where it lands, and when the monk answers it lands at Linji's, strikes him across the back for forgetting himself.
